fundamentals.pe_assessment: Trailing P/E of 31.2x is a ~37% premium to TSM's own 5-year median of 22.8x, so the stock is not cheap on backward-looking earnings. But forward P/E of 19.0x implies roughly 60%+ earnings growth already visible in estimates, and a sub-20x multiple on a business compounding revenue >40% with 50.8% operating margins is undemanding. Price of $413.41 sits 13.7% below the 52w high of $479.00 and 31% below the $542.64 street target.
fundamentals.margin_analysis: Margins are best-in-class for the foundry industry: 59.9% gross, 50.8% operating, 44.6% net. Advanced-node mix (3nm/5nm) and pricing power are carrying structural gross margin above the company's own long-term ~53% target. The clear watch item is management's guided 2-4pp consolidated gross margin dilution from overseas fabs (Arizona, Kumamoto); even at the low end of ~56%, margins stay exceptional, and Arizona's NT$36.1bn H1 2026 profit vs NT$16.1bn for all of 2025 suggests overseas dilution is running better than feared.
fundamentals.debt_analysis: Balance sheet is fortress-grade: total debt of NT$1.065tn against NT$5.355tn equity is a debt/equity ratio of just 19.9%, and debt is only ~0.63x a single year's net income (NT$1.698tn). Free cash flow of NT$992bn covers the entire debt load in roughly one year. FCF conversion of ~58% of net income is the one soft spot, but that is a deliberate consequence of the $60-64bn FY2026 capex, not financial stress.
fundamentals.growth_outlook: Growth is accelerating, not decelerating. July 2026 revenue of NT$467.58bn set a record at +44.7% YoY, and management guides FY2026 USD revenue growth 'slightly above 40%'. Capex raised to $60-64bn with 70-80% directed at advanced nodes, three new 3nm fabs (Taiwan, Arizona, Kumamoto) and 5nm-to-3nm conversions, signals demand visibility well into 2027 rather than a cyclical peak. Analyst distribution is uniformly constructive and drifting more positive (strongBuy 5 to 6, hold 2 to 1 over three months) with zero sell ratings.

fundamentals.summary: TSM is the indispensable supplier to the AI compute buildout, and at 19.0x forward earnings the market is paying a modest multiple for accelerating 40%+ revenue growth, 50.8% operating margins, and a balance sheet carrying just 19.9% debt/equity. The trailing 31.2x P/E versus a 22.8x historical median is the main valuation caution, and guided 2-4pp gross margin dilution from overseas fabs is a real headwind — though Arizona's H1 2026 profit of NT$36.1bn versus NT$16.1bn for all of 2025 suggests that dilution is proving milder than feared. Buy with high confidence; ~31% implied upside to the $542.64 street target, with the principal risk being geopolitical rather than fundamental.

sentiment.news_summary: Fundamental news is strongly positive — July revenue set a record at NT$467.58bn (+44.7% YoY) with FY2026 guided slightly above +40% in USD, and Arizona already contributed NT$36.1bn of H1-2026 profit versus NT$16.1bn for all of 2025. The offsetting narratives are valuation and margin: a 4.1% single-day drop on 2026-08-18 tied to sector profit-taking and a trailing P/E above 28x vs a 22.8x 5-year median, GuruFocus flagging ~26.7% overvaluation against GF Value $326.37 (while scoring 97/100 on quality), and management guiding 2-4pp of potential consolidated gross-margin compression as $60-64bn of capex scales three new 3nm fabs. Analyst positioning is uniformly constructive with zero sell ratings across four months and one hold upgraded to strongBuy over the last two.

sentiment.summary: Sentiment is mixed but tilted positive: the fundamental tape (record +44.7% YoY July revenue, Arizona profitability inflecting, unanimous analyst support with zero sell ratings) is running well ahead of the price action, which is being driven by valuation compression and margin anxiety rather than any deterioration in demand. Sentiment here looks behind the fundamentals on growth and possibly ahead of them on margin risk — the 2-4pp overseas gross-margin drag is real and recurring, and a 28x trailing multiple leaves little cushion. The contrarian caveat is that unanimity (19 of 19 non-sell, targets 31% above spot) is itself a warning that the positive case is fully subscribed, which caps this at buy with medium confidence rather than strong_buy.

technical.trend: Longer-term uptrend intact (price 13.7% above SMA-200 of 363.53 and above SMA-20), but the intermediate trend has rolled over — price 413.41 sits below the falling-to-flat SMA-50 at 424.79 after a sharp -4.1% reversal from the 430.97 close on 08-17.
technical.rsi_assessment: At 71.14 RSI is marginally overbought, having just pushed through the 70 threshold on the 08-12 to 08-17 advance. In a structural uptrend this reads more as momentum strength than an outright sell trigger, but the fact that RSI is elevated while price simultaneously broke down through SMA-50 is a bearish divergence in behaviour — momentum readings have not yet caught down to the 08-18 price rejection, so expect RSI to fade toward the 50s if 410 fails.
technical.macd_assessment: MACD line 1.4202 has crossed above the signal at -0.5806, producing a positive histogram of +2.0008 — a fresh bullish crossover confirming the recovery off the 374.67 low on 07-29. However, this crossover is lagging: it reflects the 08-12 to 08-17 rally and does not incorporate the 08-18 breakdown, so the histogram is likely to compress in the coming sessions.
technical.volume_assessment: Volume ratio 1.1362 (13.98M vs 20-day average 12.30M) shows the 08-18 decline came on above-average, expanding volume, while the preceding rally into 430.97 was made on notably declining volume (9.53M to 6.29M between 08-12 and 08-14). That combination — rally on thinning volume, selloff on expanding volume — is distribution-flavoured and argues against chasing strength here.
technical.summary: TSM remains in a long-term uptrend (+86.9% off the 52-week low, well above SMA-200) but has just been rejected at the SMA-50 at 424.79, with the 08-18 breakdown to 413.41 coming on above-average volume after a rally built on shrinking volume. RSI at 71.1 and the fresh positive MACD histogram both reflect the now-broken advance rather than current conditions, and bb_pct of 0.51 places price mid-channel with ATR-14 at 13.50 leaving room in either direction. Neutral pending resolution: reclaiming 424.79 restores the buy case, while a close below 410.77 opens 398-406 and then the 384.92 lower band.

macro.fed_impact: The Fed held at 3.50%-3.75% on 2026-07-29 with a hawkish 9-3 split (Hammack, Kashkari, Logan all dissenting for a 25bp HIKE) and language that inflation remains elevated versus the 2% goal, partly from energy/supply shocks. For TSM this is a mild valuation headwind rather than a business headwind: a beta of 1.258 means a higher-for-longer or hawkish-tilting discount rate compresses the multiple on a long-duration semiconductor name, and there is no August FOMC, so 2026-09-15/16 is the next catalyst and a live hike risk. Operationally the rate path matters little — TSMC funds its $60-64bn FY2026 capex overwhelmingly from operating cash flow, so its cost of capital is far less rate-sensitive than that of leveraged cyclicals.
macro.interest_rate_outlook: Base case is an extended hold: the FOMC is split with the dissent skewed hawkish, so the near-term risk is asymmetric toward a hike or a longer plateau rather than cuts, with September the first decision point. A higher-for-longer real rate keeps pressure on high-multiple tech, but is not a demand signal for leading-edge AI capacity, which is being funded by hyperscaler cash flow. If the hawkish dissenters win in September, expect multiple compression across semis that hits TSM's share price more than its earnings.
macro.fx_impact: USD/TWD is around 31.94 as of 2026-08-18, having eased from roughly 32.41 on 2026-08-04 (TWD +~1.1% over the past month) but with TWD still down about 6% over twelve months. Net currency effect is a translation tailwind: TSMC bills a large share of sales in USD while reporting in TWD, so a structurally weaker TWD inflates reported TWD revenue and gross margin. The offsets are that overseas fabs in Arizona and Kumamoto carry USD/JPY-denominated cost bases that dilute that benefit, and that August's TWD recovery could reverse the tailwind quickly. BNM policy and MYR are not applicable here — TSM is a US-listed ADR over a Taiwan-domiciled company.
sector_macro_factors: AI capex supercycle is the dominant macro driver and is still accelerating: July 2026 revenue of NT$467.58bn was TSMC's highest month on record and management raised the 2026 outlook
FY2026 capex of $60-64bn is a demand signal from the customer side but also a fixed-cost commitment that raises the earnings hit if the AI cycle rolls over

Semiconductor tariff regime is now a competitive moat: the 2026-01-15 US-Taiwan trade agreement gives Taiwanese chipmakers expanding US production reduced or excluded Section 232 tariffs, rewarding TSMC's Arizona build-out
The 10% Section 122 surcharge on semiconductors is a residual cost/pricing friction that must be passed through or absorbed in margin
Sector beta of 1.258 and a ~$2.14tn market cap make TSM a de facto macro-liquidity proxy
Energy prices are explicitly called out in the FOMC statement as an inflation source; fabs are extremely power-intensive
Geographic diversification into Arizona, Kumamoto and Germany raises the blended cost curve versus Taiwan-only production
geopolitical_risks: Cross-strait tension remains the single largest tail risk and is not priced linearly; the ADR structure gives US holders no protection
US export-control volatility toward China has been erratic in 2026 — H200 banned, unbanned, then hit with a 25% tariff — plus a new licensing framework
Taiwan has tightened its own export controls, adding 279 entities to a strategic high-tech watch list
The January 2026 US-Taiwan Section 232 relief is contingent on continued US expansion and could be revoked
Customer concentration intersects with policy risk — the largest AI accelerator customers are themselves subject to China export licensing
Japan and Germany fab expansion adds subsidy-dependency risk
Concentration of advanced packaging (CoWoS) capacity in Taiwan means even a non-military disruption is a global supply shock
macro.summary: The dated macro picture is a mild valuation headwind against a strong fundamental tailwind: the Fed is on hold at 3.50%-3.75% with three hawkish dissents favoring a hike, so a beta-1.258, $2.14tn semiconductor name faces multiple-compression risk into the 2026-09-15/16 FOMC, but AI demand is macro-insensitive at present. FX is a net positive, with USD/TWD near 31.94 and TWD still ~6% weaker year-over-year flattering TWD-reported revenue on largely USD-denominated sales, while the January 2026 US-Taiwan trade agreement turns tariff policy into a relative advantage for TSMC's onshored capacity. Signal is buy at medium confidence — the demand and policy setup is favorable, but a hawkish-leaning Fed, the 10% Section 122 surcharge, erratic China export licensing, and an unpriceable cross-strait tail risk cap conviction below strong_buy.
